transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Lucid), Carlos Rivera (Lucid ML Eng), Priya Nair (Lucid Sec)

Summary: quick sync to go over quality eval numbers since we flipped to the q4 quantized build; a couple of prompt families saw a dip and we want to triage.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — everyone can hear ok?
[00:03] Maya: yep can hear you, thanks.
[00:05] Jordan: cool. agenda is the same: go through the eval spreadsheet, call out regressions, decide what to re-run and set owners. samira i know you ran the regression overnight?
[00:14] Samira: yeah i kicked off the full suite, and i pulled out the prompt families that dropped more than 5 points. overall model is fine but three clusters, notably the "dosage guidance" prompts, dropped from about .87 to .81. there are also a handful of hallucination-ish outputs where dates got mangled.
[00:28] Carlos: yeah we saw that in prod — some responses now say "recommend 2 tablets daily starting 2024" which is wrong, weird date formatting. might be tokenizer related with the quantized kernels.
[00:38] Samira: possible, could also be the system prompt truncation with the smaller kv cache heuristics, we've seen off-by-one in cache rotation.
[00:46] Priya: from security side, we also noticed that the content filter flagged a few legitimate clinical QAs as safety hits, causing partial responses. that's blocking a small % of requests.
[00:58] Jordan: okay good, so we have two threads: quality regressions (dates/hallucinations) and guardrail false positive behavior. samira what's the top hypothesis for the quality drop?
[01:07] Samira: primary hypothesis is the quantization profile q4-plus we switched to — subtle changes to attention scaling and kernel rounding can shift token probabilities, which cascades in long prompt contexts. second hypothesis is batching timing changed and some system tokens are being clipped.
[01:21] Maya: is this something you'd expect to see fixed by prompt engineering or do we need to revert to the previous model?
[01:26] Samira: short term we can try prompt-level mitigations: stronger system instruction anchors, add guardrail checks that post-process dates, and reduce temperature a bit. we should also run a delta test: previous fp32 baseline vs current q4 run on the same 2k prompt holdout.
[01:41] Jordan: okay let's do the delta test. samira can you rerun with the baseline and the q4 variant and produce a side-by-side CSV?
[01:48] Samira: yes — i'll include the per-prompt PPL-ish score and our composite quality metric; should have that by saturday.
[01:55] Carlos: i can attach the prod traces for the failure requests, that might help — i'll pull 50 examples.
[02:00] Jordan: perfect. on the guardrail false positives — priya, can you show examples?
[02:05] Priya: sure — i pasted three cases in the shared sheet. the filter flagged answers that mentioned medication names with the word "risk" even when the context was a safety explanation. it looked like the safety classifier threshold is conservative.
[02:17] Samira: that sounds like a threshold tuning; we can add a whitelist for clinical terms or use a second-stage classifier with higher context. also function-calling could help, returning structured fields instead of free text reduces false triggers.
[02:29] Maya: is function-calling supported in the dedicated path?
[02:32] Jordan: yes — function/tool calling works across hosted and dedicated. if you want structured outputs we'll wire up the schema and run the eval. note: structured responses may require prompt adjustments.
[02:41] Carlos: what about latency impact if we switch to dedicated or keep hosted? the quantized model is cheaper but we're seeing these regressions.
[02:49] Jordan: tradeoffs: q4 quantized helps cost but can introduce small quality shifts; dedicated gives predictable throughput but doesn't magically fix quantization artifacts. if you need absolute parity with fp32, we can offer a mixed policy: use fp32 for the prompt families you care about and q4 for others.
[03:04] Maya: that mixed approach sounds promising — can you estimate cost delta?
[03:07] Jordan: i'll run numbers for a 10k RPM commit and show the per-token cost difference for mixed routing vs all-q4 by monday.
[03:14] Priya: also two security items — we need confirmation on KMS key ownership and whether logs will have any PHI redaction by default.
[03:21] Jordan: noted. we'll confirm KMS options (customer-managed keys supported) and default logging retention; i'll include options for redaction and PII scrubbing in the security doc.
[03:31] Samira: for immediate triage i propose: 1) rerun delta suite (fp32 vs q4) 2) run targeted prompt-level temperature sweep and system prompt anchors 3) add a second-stage classifier on the flagged families and log full context for false positives.
[03:45] Carlos: we can help label the 500 prompts if you want, that'll speed up classifier tuning.
[03:48] Maya: yes we can label. also can we get a prioritized list of prompt families to focus on?
[03:53] Samira: i'll send a ranked list, top 10 families by impact.
[03:57] Jordan: ok last part — timeline and owners.
[04:00] Jordan: recap: samira reruns regression and sends csv by 2026-10-17; jordan sends pricing and updated eval sheet today; carlos shares 50 prod failure logs by 2026-10-16; priya and jordan schedule security deep-dive by 2026-10-20.
[04:15] Maya: sounds good. anything else?
[04:18] Carlos: quick question — do you have a recommended system prompt for clinical QAs to reduce hallucinations?
[04:23] Samira: yes, we have a template — short anchor instructions, explicit date formatting rules, and an "if uncertain, ask for clarification" fallback. i'll paste it in the sheet.
[04:32] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up over email and update the sheet.
[04:36] Maya: thanks all.
[04:38] Jordan: bye.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Redwood to share updated eval spreadsheet and system prompt templates (Jordan)
- Samira to rerun regression suite (fp32 vs q4) and produce per-prompt CSV (due 2026-10-17)
- Carlos to provide 50 prod failure examples and logs (due 2026-10-16)
- Priya and Jordan to schedule security deep-dive covering VPC, KMS, retention, redaction (by 2026-10-20)
- Customer to label 500 prompts for second-stage classifier (target 2026-10-21)
